# Run command / script (`command.run`)

**Kind:** action · **Category:** Apps & scripts · **Runs as:** depends on the fields (see below) · **Revertible:** no

Runs a PowerShell script or a command line.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | text (multi-line) | yes |  | The script or command line. Details of the event are available as environment variables, e.g. $env:AUTOSETTINGS_USER and $env:AUTOSETTINGS_APP_PATH in PowerShell or %AUTOSETTINGS_USER% in cmd ({{ placeholders }} are deliberately not replaced in scripts). |
| `shell` | one of: `powershell`, `pwsh`, `cmd`, `none` | no | `powershell` | powershell (Windows PowerShell 5.1), pwsh (PowerShell 7), cmd, or none (run the command line directly). |
| `run_as` | one of: `user`, `system` | no | `user` | user runs as the signed-in user; system runs as the local SYSTEM account (machine automations only). |
| `wait` | true / false | no | `false` | Wait for the command to finish before the next action. A non-zero exit code then counts as a failure. |
| `timeout` | duration (`30s`, `5m`, `1h30m`) | no | `1m` | When waiting, stop the command after this long. |
| `hidden` | true / false | no | `true` | Run without showing a console window. |
| `continue_on_error` | true / false | no | `false` | Keep running the next actions even if this one fails. |

## Example

```yaml
actions:
  - type: command.run
    shell: powershell
    command: |
      Stop-Process -Name OneDrive -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

## Notes

Every [placeholder](../placeholders.md) is available to the script as an environment variable named AUTOSETTINGS_ followed by the placeholder name in capitals with dots replaced by underscores: {{ user }} → AUTOSETTINGS_USER, {{ app.path }} → AUTOSETTINGS_APP_PATH. Placeholders are not replaced inside the script text itself, because window titles and file names are chosen by other programs and could otherwise inject commands. Scripts in machine automations can only be edited by administrators, because they may run as SYSTEM.
